# Compute Atlas

> Open, source-cited map and dataset of grid-scale compute infrastructure across the United States, including data centers, AI/ML-oriented campuses, crypto-mining sites, and related dedicated power-generation facilities.

Last reviewed: 2026-09-29

## Canonical

- Website: https://www.compute-atlas.com/
- Statistics: https://www.compute-atlas.com/stats
- API documentation: https://www.compute-atlas.com/api
- Methodology: https://www.compute-atlas.com/docs/methodology

## Public API

No authentication is required for public read endpoints:

- GET https://www.compute-atlas.com/api/facilities
- GET https://www.compute-atlas.com/api/facilities/{id}
- GET https://www.compute-atlas.com/api/stats
- GET https://www.compute-atlas.com/api/schema

Use the live API or dataset for counts instead of copying totals into answers, because facility and state counts change as the dataset is reviewed.

## Evidence model

Every live facility must have at least one citable public source. Records expose confidence and provenance rather than hiding uncertainty.

Core rules:
- no fact without a source;
- unknown fields are omitted rather than guessed;
- consequential claims are checked against the underlying filing or announcement;
- proposed changes enter a pending staging queue;
- human approval is required before a facility becomes live;
- approved changes are recorded in an audit trail.

## Scope boundaries

- A record can be confirmed, reported, or otherwise explicitly qualified by the dataset. Preserve that qualification.
- Eligibility for an incentive is not the same as a confirmed award.
- A modeled range or project ceiling is not the same as an observed value.
- The atlas is a research dataset for journalists, researchers, local officials, and residents, not a government registry.
- For current counts and individual facility status, prefer the live API and cited primary sources.
